subject: Animation
title: Killing Your Darlings at Pixar
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Killing Your Darlings at Pixar.

hook.text: Pixar has scrapped entire films deep into production when the story was not working.

buildup.text: Ratatouille lost its original director eight months before release. Pixar rebuilt it from scratch.

discovery.text: Brave and The Good Dinosaur both underwent massive overhauls that cost the studio years and millions.

twist.text: Most studios would ship a flawed film to recoup costs. Pixar chooses to eat the loss and start over.

climax.text: This willingness to restart is expensive but ensures Pixar rarely releases a film it does not believe in.

punchline.text: Pixar would rather lose money than release a bad story.

quiz.question: What does Pixar do when a film's story is not working during production?
options: They release it anyway to avoid financial loss
They scrap and rebuild the film, even deep into production, absorbing the cost
They hand it off to Disney to finish

details.summary: Pixar is famous for drastically reworking or scrapping entire films that are not working, even late in production. Ratatouille, Brave, and The Good Dinosaur all underwent fundamental creative overhauls, demonstrating Pixar's commitment to story quality over sunk costs.
details.whyItMatters: Willingness to restart is Pixar's most painful but valuable creative practice. Ignoring sunk-cost fallacy — the money already spent — in favor of story quality separates good studios from great ones.
takeaways: Pixar has restarted or fundamentally reworked multiple films mid-production
Ratatouille, Brave, and The Good Dinosaur all underwent major creative overhauls
Prioritizing story quality over sunk costs is central to Pixar's creative philosophy

faq.question: Which Pixar films were significantly reworked during production?
faq.answer: Ratatouille replaced its director and was substantially rewritten by Brad Bird. Brave replaced Brenda Chapman as director. The Good Dinosaur was restarted almost from scratch. Toy Story 2 was drastically reworked in nine months. Each case prioritized the final film over prior investment.

faq.question: How does Pixar justify the cost of restarting films?
faq.answer: A mediocre Pixar film damages the brand more than the cost of a restart. Each film carries the weight of audience expectations built over decades. Spending extra to get a film right protects the billions of dollars in brand value that Pixar's quality reputation represents.
